fit: Four source-user deletion submodels, each uses remaining3users. Four random-row deletion submodels match each domain deletion retained class counts exactly. Refit source-only mean/scale/intercept and weighted ridge for each mask, lambda inherited unchanged from full-source onehot validation selection. Encoder frozen and trained on all4source users.
random_masks: For each held h, deleted user d, class k: RNG SeedSequence([seed,h,d,k]); choose without replacement from full source IDs the same number of IDs as domain deletion removes from that class. Sort retained IDs.
aggregation: Per-class minimum of four raw onehot ridge scores is primary domain_min; arithmetic mean control. Same min and mean of four class-count-matched random deletion readouts. Full original ridge unchanged. No temperature, probabilities, calibration or uncertainty multiplier.
interpretation: min equals worst expected class score over any convex mixture of four fixed deletion models. No generalization bound or confidence coverage; source model sensitivities correlated and encoder still saw each deleted user.
scope: six reused development users3..8, source4/next validation/held diagnostic. Inductive per-clip head robustness screen, not original contribution.
stop: Failure closes this fixed deletion/minimum/normalization/seed/lambda configuration. No mixture weights, quantile, uncertainty penalty or seed sweep; no eightfold expansion, no secondary-arm promotion.
limitations: Source-only training labels may be accessed; no validation/diagnostic fitting or score selection.
Missing user6 class3 can change per-class and per-user weights; matching row deletion class counts does not guarantee causal isolation of user identity.
This is not out-of-fold encoder training or full unseen-user ensemble.
Bagging/pasting, worst-case aggregation and jackknife concepts are established; original OSR docs also mention support-sample jackknife calibration.
A successful source screen only permits a separately preregistered8fold study with the94.897727% strong frozen-ridge control; not independent test.
